rules.title: Application screening fee cap ($30, CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a rental applicant a screening fee only up to the actual out-of-pocket cost of gathering information about the applicant. The fee can never exceed $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI since January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually from 1998-01-01; not more than actual out-of-pocket costs
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property, and their agents, who charge applicants (including guarantors/cosigners) a nonrefundable screening fee.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt rules governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Federal/state housing assistance program fee rules not preempted

rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: The document does not state an original effective date; CPI adjustment runs from January 1, 1998. The current CPI-adjusted dollar amount is not stated.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee when they know, or should have known, that no rental unit is available now or will be available within a reasonable time.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt rules governing deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Screening fee allowed only with first-in-time process or full refund
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a screening fee only if they offer one of two processes. Option A: consider completed applications in the order received under written screening criteria, approve the first qualified applicant, and charge no fee until an application is actually considered. Option B: refund the full fee to every unselected applicant within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission, whichever first (refund option)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents who collect application screening fees.
rules.exemptions: No refund is owed under the first-in-time option to an applicant denied after consideration for failing the screening criteria. Fees inadvertently collected from concurrent applications must be refunded within 7 days, or applied to another unit at the applicant's option.

rules.title: Itemized receipt, return of unused fee, and copy of credit report
rules.requirement: The landlord must give the applicant an itemized receipt for the screening fee and return any portion not used for authorized screening. If a fee was paid, the landlord must give the applicant a copy of their consumer credit report within seven days of receiving it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property and their agents who collect application screening fees.
rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
